(1) Format: REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION headers are present and well-formed; FINAL_STATES: u4 is nonempty, declared in STATES, and is the accepting goal state reached on target_picked_up. (2) Ordered coverage: the four task milestones each get a dedicated transition — u0 blocker_moved -> u1 (+0.1), u1 (has_door_key & blocker_moved) -> u2 (+0.2), u2 (door_open & has_door_key) -> u3 (+0.3), u3 target_picked_up -> u4 (+1.0) — matching 'move ball before key', 'open door with key', and 'pick up the box'. Requiring blocker_moved to hold again at the key-pickup step correctly enforces the ball-away-before-key ordering at the moment the key is taken, not just 'ever moved'. (3) Irrelevant events: every state has a per-state else self-loop, so all other valuations (turns, moves, no-op drops, impossible-before-constraint events like door_open in u0/u1 or target_picked_up before u3) are absorbed without spurious transitions. (4) Event/condition distinction: key_lost is used only as a one-step trigger with self-loop penalties (-0.2) in u0, u1, u2 — exactly the states where it can fire (door closed); it is correctly omitted in u3/u4 where door_open makes it impossible. blocker_moved is treated as a condition, so re-blocking the ball suspends progress rather than corrupting state, and the u1 key_lost rule is reachable (re-block, take key, drop key) and penalized consistently with 'try not to drop the key while the door is still closed'. (5) Reward safety: all progress rewards are earned at most once (no u1->u0, u2->u1, or u3->u2 back edges, so no farming of 0.1/0.2/0.3); re-picking the key inside u2 hits else with zero reward; totals are bounded (max 1.6, monotone increasing 0.1/0.2/0.3/1.0) and the only negatives are agent-controlled key_lost penalties. (6) Label determinism: no step can satisfy two outgoing labels of the same state — key_lost excludes has_door_key and requires a closed door, contradicting door_open; blocker_moved cannot co-occur with key_lost in u0 (ball never picked up while in u0); and the door-opening step necessarily occurs while the RM is in u2, so the u1 conjunctions never collide with door_open. (7) No stuck states: every non-final state retains a realizable path to u4 (e.g., u1 with the ball re-blocked and key held: drop key, re-move ball, re-take key). Minor notes, non-blocking: the has_door_key conjunct in the u2->u3 label is technically redundant given the door_open-after-has_door_key constraint, but it usefully makes 'open the door with the key' explicit; the key-first ordering violation is penalized indirectly via the guaranteed key_lost drop rather than at pickup, which is consistent with the environment's account that key-first necessarily fires key_lost while the door is closed. No rewrite needed.
